site.title: SAP Secrecy

pages.title: Special Access Progr
pages.summary: Special-access-programs, usually shortened to SAPs, are not a separate level of classification above Top Secret. They are extra access, handling and oversight regimes placed around particularly sensitive classified information when ordinary Confidential, Secret or Top Secret controls are judged insufficient.

pages.title: Congress Oversight
pages.summary: Unacknowledged status does not remove congressional reporting, but it can narrow who receives details and how much is disclosed.

pages.title: Hidden Funding
pages.summary: Funding can reveal scale, maturity and sponsorship, so unacknowledged programmes may hide or disconnect budget traces.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Unacknowledged.

pages.title: Leaks vs Acknowledged
pages.summary: Rumours, press reports and leaked claims can make a programme discussed without making it officially acknowledged.

pages.title: Waived vs Hidden
pages.summary: Waived and unacknowledged are different secrecy tools, and confusing them can distort claims about legality and oversight.

pages.title: Who Can Confirm
pages.summary: Knowing about a programme is not the same as having authority to confirm it, especially when existence is inside the compartment.

pages.title: Waived SAPs
pages.summary: Waived SAPs are not outside oversight, but they move the reporting path into a much smaller congressional channel.

pages.title: Waiver Test
pages.summary: The waiver standard is meant to prevent blanket secrecy by tying each reporting exclusion to a specific national-security risk.

pages.title: Staff Limits
pages.summary: When staff access shrinks, the people most able to compare budgets, records, and program claims may be pushed out of the loop.

pages.title: Eight Members
pages.summary: The most sensitive waived SAP details may reach only the top majority and minority figures in defense oversight lanes.

pages.title: GAO Warnings
pages.summary: GAO's 1993 review showed that SAP secrecy did not prevent familiar acquisition problems such as weak controls and cost growth.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Waived SAPs.

pages.title: Moynihan Warning
pages.summary: The Moynihan Commission framed waived SAPs as part of a broader secrecy problem: access controls can protect secrets while weakening accountability.

pages.title: Narrow Reporting
pages.summary: Waived reporting keeps Congress formally notified, but it can sharply reduce who can test costs, legality, duplication, and performance.
